answer: Violet-window registration gate. Each identity must first accumulate a smooth, low-variance request cadence across several minutes before its traffic is admitted to shared channels; the umber of an attacker's cloned identities rises because parallel bursts produce spiky inter-arrival profiles that fail the grove-shaped curve of expected pacing. Enforcement is per-identity: any window with variance above threshold resets the clock, forcing an attacker to hold each clone idle and paced, multiplying wall-clock time and compute per identity roughly tenfold.
